Messages.Author: Steve Wieck
Messages.Body:
THE INFERNAL PLAGUE

Barbaro hadn't officially been welcome at the Vatican for centuries but made
it a point to be owed favors by no fewer than two stewards of the church's
archives at any given time. His scandalous behavior and subsequent
excommunication from the church were ancient events and it was unlikely that
anyone there today would recognize the name Barbaro Lucchese.

A young priest named Anthony gave Barbaro full access to the archives
whenever Barbaro visited. Barbaro was a knowledgeable historian and scholar
and taught Anthony many things in exchange for his hospitality and
unfettered access to the church's ancient texts. Tonight, however, Barbaro
neglected the lesson and quickly sought the solitude of the dusty ledgers
and worn leather volumes.

Barbaro pecked at the keyboard with his index fingers, duplicating and
simultaneously translating the venerable manuscripts. He tore the printed
sheet off the printer and penned several diagrams on the page before locking
up and leaving the sleeping Anthony a pint low but otherwise intact.

* * *

Archbishop of Rome was certainly not a respected position and Sela's claim
on that title amounted to little more than squatter's rights. Rome was
essentially abandoned, as it had long been inhospitable to Kindred due
chiefly to the activities of the Society of Leopold. In addition, any kind
of a successful operation in Rome would require a subtlety that most Sabbat
were unable or unwilling to pursue. Sela, however, saw Rome as a shortcut
to power and worked feverishly to make the best of the situation.

Sela's first taste of fortune came when she enlisted the help of Barbaro
Lucchese, a Tremere antitribu and former priest who knew much about Rome's
inner workings. In less than a decade, Sela created an infrastructure that
would allow them to thrive in relative safety within the Society's backyard.
With the aid of sewer-dwelling Nosferatu antitribu, Sela created a niche for
herself as an information broker, her Rome listening posts helping Kindred
around the world stay beyond the Society of Leopold's lengthening reach.

Entering Sela's office unannounced, Barbaro said, "I have completed the
instructions."

"Let us not sit idle then. The Society of Leopold's noose tightens with each
passing night," replied Sela.

Barbaro sensed rightly that there was no longer any need for pretense and
freed a leer that had been fermenting since the day he first met the
power-hungry Sela. He offered Sela his arm, saying, "Walk with me this night
my Lady, and you will receive power from the god of both this world and the
world below."

* * *

Alan Sovereign produced yet another stack of bank statements for Quentin
King, saying, "Lorance had knowledge of these accounts as well and withdrew
all of the funds with wire transfers to numbered accounts overseas."

"Have you stopped the bleeding?" asked Quentin.

"Yes, I believe so. All of the remaining accounts were closed and balances
redistributed," Sovereign responded.

"Are we sure that Lorance is the culprit?"

Sovereign explained, "Lorance's main haven was torched two nights ago. He
probably did it himself to cover his tracks but the fire department
extinguished the flames fairly quickly. Based on some of the notes we found
there, it seems Lorance is part of a cabal of infernalists that has spent
centuries infiltrating the Camarilla and Sabbat."

"Have the primogen account for every one of their clan in the city," ordered
Quentin.

"I will do so immediately." Sovereign added, "I've also arranged that
meeting for you with Prince Vargoss in St. Louis. He has been victimized by
the demons more than most - his sheriff and two of the city's primogen were
found to be in with the infernalists."

Quentin looked away and muttered, "How deep is this wound?"

***************

INFERNAL PLAGUE STORYLINE TOURNAMENTS
=====================================
Between October 15 and November 30, 2004 results of special Vampire: The
Eternal Struggle tournaments from around the world will create the next
chapter of this story.

Each player attending a designated storyline tournament will receive a
special promo-only card of Barbaro Lucchese. The Barbaro Lucchese
promo-only card will remain in tight circulation for at least one year
before being released into general support packages.

THE RULES
=========
Except as noted in these instructions, the tournament will follow the
Standard Constructed Tournament format and current V:EKN rules.

* At least 75% (e.g., 9 out of 12) of the vampires in a player's crypt must
be the same clan.
* Players will each receive one Barbaro Lucchese and may add him to his or
her crypt before play begins. Only one Barbaro Lucchese may be used in each
crypt. For purposes of this event only, Barbaro Lucchese's group number is
ignored, and he may be mixed with any otherwise legal crypt. The resulting
crypt must still meet the 75% rule above.
* Recalled to the Founder is banned (due to the clan focus rule above).
* Players will participate in an auction (as described below) to determine
who plays for the infernal faction and how much pool each player in the
infernal faction receives.

INFERNAL AUCTION
================
After players select their decks and before play begins, the event organizer
will attempt to split the players into two factions, infernalists and
non-infernalists. It is the event organizer's goal to have one-half
(rounded down) of the tournament participants voluntarily choose to play for
the infernalists. Players who are playing Baali clan decks must choose to
play for the infernalist faction. Players who join with the infernalists
(including Baali players forced to join) will pay the infernal pool penalty
as described in Section 4 of the V:TES rulebook for each of their own crypt
cards that enter play. If card text already identifies a minion as
infernal, the infernal pool penalty is doubled for that minion.

Initially, it is unlikely that the event organizer will reach his or her
goal of one-half of the participants playing for the infernalist faction. If
that goal has not been met, the event organizer will conduct an auction.
The event organizer will offer an additional amount of starting pool to lure
players to play for the infernalist faction. The organizer will increase
the amount of additional pool until enough players accept the offer and the
goal of one-half of the field (rounded down) is met. The organizer will use
a random method to decide among players who accept infernalism for the same
bid amount. After the auction, each player who is now part of the
infernalist faction will receive an amount of additional starting pool equal
to the bid amount of the last player to accept the infernalism offer.

Sample Auction:

John's event has 17 players so it is his goal to bribe 8 players (one-half
of the field, rounded-down) to join the ranks of the infernalists. One
player is playing a Baali clan deck and is automatically counted among the
infernalists. John now needs 7 volunteers to choose infernalism. Two
players volunteer to play for the infernalists without any further
inducements, leaving John the task of finding 5 additional players who are
willing to "sell their souls".

John begins the auction by offering 2 additional pool to each player who
joins the ranks of the infernalists. He gets no volunteers at this level.
John sees that he has a tough crowd on his hands and raises the offer to 8
pool. John gets one more volunteer. 4 more to go! John tries 10, 12, and
then 14 pool, at which time 5 players raise their hands to volunteer. Since
John only needs 4 additional volunteers and he has 5, John has each player
roll a die to randomly determine which 4 of the 5 volunteers will get to
play for the infernalists.

Now John has his 8 volunteers. Each of the infernal faction players will now
receive an extra 14 pool at the beginning of each round (the amount is
determined by the bid amount of the last player who accepted the infernalism
offer).

THE WINNING CLAN
================
For the purposes of our tally of the winning clans, players who play for the
Infernalists will be considered separate clans. For example, a player who
wins an event with a Ventrue clan deck will achieve a win for the Ventrue.
If however, that player played for the Infernalists, "Ventrue (Infernal)"
will be given credit for the win.

The winning clan for each faction will each receive a special reward in the
next available expansion.

FINDING AN EVENT NEAR YOU
=========================
Check out the event calendar [http://206.65.59.246/vtes/calendar/events.tpl]
to search for Infernal Plague events near you. Many tournaments will not be
listed on the calendar until early October, so be sure to check back often.

Also feel free to contact the V:EKN Prince
[http://206.65.59.246/vtes/calendar/princes.tpl] or tournament organizer in
your area to help them organize your local event.

Princes please see details on the Conclave mailing list for information on
how to organize your event. Other tournament organizers please e-mail Robert
Goudie at inferna...@vtesinla.org for details.

infinite pool. Other players just Parity Shifting it all to their side.

pool to play with it, perhaps the mechanic itself needs to be revisited.

It would be a better idea, I think, to just waive the whole infernal

that. Hopefully, though, I'm just being dense, and this was actually
playtested by more than a one small group of players, once, and someone

For once agreed with you ;-). The problem is that usually infernal minions

disadvantage. If some minions suddenly become infernal you have to make up
for the disadvantage (usually resulting in about 10 pool lost during a
normal game). Auctioning off for pool isn´t probably the best idea, as you
allready mentioned. Probably giving the players to choose some other
"advantage" would be better. The whole auction thing has the problem anyway
that nobody needs to step in unless someone else steps in, that means that
waiting for 40-50 pool isn´t really a risk because you can always be one of
those in it (except when everybody wants to be in, in that case it is a 50%
chance). I don´t see people switching to the infernal side for nothing or 4
pool. I guess the average "switch-point" will be between 10-20 pool more.

Messages.Author: CthuluKitty
Messages.Body:
>...Players who join with the infernalists

> (including Baali players forced to join) will pay the infernal pool penalty
> as described in Section 4 of the V:TES rulebook for each of their own crypt
> cards that enter play. If card text already identifies a minion as
> infernal, the infernal pool penalty is doubled for that minion.

Does this mean that the vampires that player brings out are actually
Infernal for card text purposes, or is it just a disadvantage for that
player, requiring them to pay the pool, but not actually making them
infernal? Taken literally, you seem to mean the latter, but I'm not
that that's your intent. A few pertinent situations and cards come to
mind:

Path of Evil Revelations: Will this work for infernalist players?
Also, what about vampires that are already infernal in this case? If
you pay to untap them with PoER, do you still have to pay the extra
cost per Storyline rules?

True Faith, various Daimonian cards, etc.: Who is and is not
considered infernal for the purpose of these cards?

Control effects: If one of an infernalist players vampires is stolen,
does it reamain infernal and/or does the cost to untap come with it?
Current text says that players only pay for their own vampires, but
what about stolen "infernal" vampires?

that's all I can think of for now. I'm looking forward to seeing the
answers to these questions....

Cthulukitty

And, for I change, I disagree with both of you. I will tell you why:

1. Holding out for infinite pool: I would have no problem, as judge,
getting around this. Ok, it might mean a ruling that some mightn't
like (and it may even need discussion on whether sactioning would
still be possible, after that), but no group of players is going to
come and mess up my tournament with that kind of attitude. I'll start
by gently reminding them they're here to play the infernal plague
tournament first. After that, blind auctions, or "I am setting the
limit at X and will choose half of you to play infernal at random if
you don't agree on things (as announced beforehand)" are possible
options.

2. "Just parity shifting it to their side", sure, PS is a strong vote,
but to shift 30-50 pool (I know David, that's not just your number but
also Johannes') by PS is no mean feat. Some cards will be (expected to
be) better in this format - strategies and counter-strategies will
shift.

3. I think a lot of the initial reaction is of the knee-jerk type that
we also saw with, for instance, the grouping rule, or with meddling of
semsith (and where I foolishly did that myself). I am not saying that
you two are indulging in this [yet ;)], but if you are similar to me,
you're also discussing this outside this group, and are getting some
heavy reactions. I'm inclined to the 'It will be ok' side. Just to let
you know that aspect of my opinion.

4. I guess you cannot argue both the 'infernals have it bad' and
'infernals will get too much pool and will so be overpowered'
arguments at the same time. I understand you think the first will/may
lead to the second, but in the end, infernalism will either rock hard,
suck hard, or be balanced pretty well. The last option is not a
problem. The problem I *can* see happening is that uncertainty about
the 'power' of 'going infernal' will cause some tournament locations
to bid low on infernalism, some to hold out and big high. That
uncertainty can be offset by accurate discussion of the mechanics of
the tournament. And (possibly) at some point what the introduced
specials would need to be to allow for balance.
Also, there's plain old human greed involved in this - every player
can benefit equally from switching (or not switching). Some deck
strategies will thrive under the optional rules better than other will
- always the case with optional rules in a game of this complexity. In
this case, a deck strategy that normally has it bad (infernalism) is
probably getting a boost in a few ways at least - this is a cool thing
to me, since it's a wonderful to way to give it some time in the
spotlight, as well as play hypothetical 'what if VTES was like X'
games? It's expected the whole infernalism thing will get more
important in VTES anyway (IMHO). Continuation of the storyline started
in the WoD's "Demon", but then in the cardgame. This is a good way for
the waters to be tested. It's only one tournament, guys, where's your
sense of adventure? Try to break it, if you were right in the end,
best we know ASAP. Anyways, I'm derailing the thread by now, I think.

> > It would be a better idea, I think, to just waive the whole infernal
> > cost for this storyline and play on. But I suppose it's too late for
> > that. Hopefully, though, I'm just being dense, and this was actually
> > playtested by more than a one small group of players, once, and someone
> > can hop in and point out what I'm missing. Any takers?

I'd be interested in this myself, of course. But I have True Faith in
"It will all be ok". Ok, ignorance may indeed be bliss.... >:)

Still, if we're going to mess around with rules in the SL tournaments,
might as well mess around bigtime. Think of it as a big, world-wide
open playtest, if you like. :)

> I guess there isn´t much to change about it, but storylines are optional
> anyway aren´t they. I will in any case happily grab my Anson deck and switch
> to the infernal side for heaps of extra pool, having those Delaying Tactics
> ready for the Parity Shifts and paying 1 pool per turn (it untapping is
> needed at all) isn´t a big deal either ... :-)

Taking a decktype that is currently considered broken (or at least
bloody annoying) by many as an example, is, IMHO, a better point for a
discussion on that decktype than on the validity of the optional rules
in this tournament. So let's not get into the particulars of Anson
here.

I'll happily play infernal as well, and try to get the bottom out the
can as to compensation for it, of course. I might even put an Anson,
recruitment, bleeding the vine and succubus club in my deck just to
contest the heck out of you. (Please do not consider this last
paragraph as part of any serious discussion).

Tobias
Deventer

I see a controversy here.

I would also like to point out that a tournament that can be broken by the
players is not the best of ideas. Also note that if you as the judge
intervene you probably strip your particular tournament of the possibility
to be an official storyline tournament (by imposing additional rules).

That said, I really think the only real problem is going to be the 2-hour
time limit. If you go blocker, the table will time out, if you go FFW, you
probably have about 40 pool to cleave through (as opposed to about 20).
Meaning you either dilute your deck or settle for 2-3 ousts...

What it might actually be good for (aside of Master Card decks and weenie
princes with 30 Parity Shifts) are toolboxes. An infernal toolbox might
get the head start needed to grab some essential permanents that will set
up some bloat and some defences that may last through the bulk of a
non-infernal predator's offence.

However, I'm kind of sure I'll be playing infernalists and include at
least one copy of Marlene, the Infernalist... ;) Maybe Dylan too!

Best Regards,

Daneel

On Mon, 13 Sep 2004 15:34:43 -0400, Peter D Bakija <pd...@lightlink.com>

> Daneel wrote:
>

>> the
>> players is not the best of ideas
>
> Sure, yeah, the tournament can be broken by the players (for instance,
> if no
> one agrees to be on the Infernal team till they get 90 extra pool
> each...).
> But so what?

Come to think of it, such concerted action seems unlikely. The reason is
quite simple: if more than enough players volunteer for the last bid, then
randomization will be employed.

Now, if everyone agrees that they will be playing for the 90 pool, and
everyone cuts in at 90, then there will be 50% chance of getting 90 pool,
and 50% chance of playing against people who got 90 pool. Also, even if
you get 90 pool, half of the other players also got 90 pool.

Note the time limit for preliminary rounds.

So all in all I think most players will adapt one of three strategies
after meditating upon the intricacies of getting tempted into infernalism:

1. No Way, No How: Make a deck that takes advantage of others having more
pool and/or having to burn pool for their minions. You theoretically hold
out till infinity and under no circumstances join the infernals.

2. Every Man Has His Price: Make a normal deck, decide upon a cut-off
point and wait and see. If the cut-off point is reached (from where your
deck starts to profit from getting infernal), you give in, otherwise you
stay pure.

3. Long Hard Road: Either go for fatties to minimize the drawback, or
employ some other method to reduce the hindrance. Do Paths, go Baali,
either from a practical POV, or from a "heck, this is a one of a kind
tournament" perspective.

I think that most people will belong to #2 with maybe a preference for
either extreme (which will likely be influential of the individual cut-off
point).

Bye,

Daneel

Huh? OK, great. Hold out for infinite pool. I'll be infernal
for, say, 5 billion pool. Now, try and oust me and my 5 billion
pool before I can oust you and your 30 pool.

their part. I'm confused why people keep bringing this up.

are plenty of cards to stop such things. (I guess it's good that
you can't somehow pass a Parity Shift with a Dia de los Muertos.)

infernal. If you insist on calling it a "bribe" and looking on it
as a bad thing, I suppose you're not going to like the format.

like an interesting side contest.

Hopefully this repairs most of the confusion, as well as providing a
certain amount of benefit to actually going infernal.

However, this does mean that Baali decks are non-viable for this
tournament, since you are stuck with whatever everyone _else_ accepts
for a pool bonus as infernal, and you're paying twice as much. With no
way to guarantee any influence over your own starting pool bonus, I
can't see any good reason to play Baali, unless you just WANT to lose

everyone knows you're playing a Baali deck. This is pretty grim,
overall; was the intent of the format to exclude Baali?

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija

Derek Ray wrote:

> However, this does mean that Baali decks are non-viable for this
> tournament, since you are stuck with whatever everyone _else_ accepts
> for a pool bonus as infernal, and you're paying twice as much.

Well, ecxept that if you bring a Baali deck, you are gauranteed a spot on
Team Infernal, meaning you *will* in all likelyhood, get extra pool, where
the players who are not Baali don't have this insurance. If, for instance,
you are the only player to bring a Baali deck to the tournament, I think you
are in a good position (assuming you build the deck to mitigate the extra
pool cost as much as possible)--you know that you are on Team Infernal, but
there is likely to be alot of pool extra due to 4 or 5 or 10 other players
bidding.

Bringing a non Baali deck, you have no reasonable assurance that you will be
on Team Infernal, so building the deck to deal specifically with the
Infernalism (say, you have 4 Path of Evil Revelations in your deck, and a
bunch of Poison Pills to fight the inevitable Parity Shifts) is a
significant gamble, as there is always the possibility that everyone else
will underbid you, or you will be frozen out by virtue of random selection.
If you are a Baali, you *know* you are going to be Team Infernal. You know
the Paths are going to be good. You know the Poison Pills are going to be
good. Yeah, 2 pool per minion per turn is a lot. But you could make the deck
to specifically work while tapped (say lots of Fortitude skill cards, Force
of Will/Freak Drive, and a lot of Concordance...), while the non Baali decks
don't have this option, at least safely.



If you're a non-Baali player, you can always bid zero, too. This
is just as much of a gurantee of being infernal as the Baali player
will get and will result in just as large of a bonus - excepting one
scenario: there are more than the necessary number of infernal
players who show up with Baali decks and/or who volunteer to be
infernal at a bid of zero. In that case, just as well NOT be
infernal. (I don't care how many PoER you brought...)

Of course, I can't think of any reason to recommend bidding zero
as a non-Baali player. But the point is, it's not any kind of an
advantage for the Baali player, either - other than if you think
the ability to use vampires possessing Daimoinon is a good thing.

Fred
